title: Oncall readiness: TP hang / no-forward-progress response (Hosted + Dedicated)
content:
Purpose
- This doc captures what SRE oncall needs to respond to TP (tensor-parallel) hangs / no-forward-progress incidents in Redwood Serving Runtime.
- Primary goals during an incident:
  1) Stop customer impact (timeouts/5xx/streaming hangs).
  2) Prevent repeated allocation of work to unhealthy TP groups.
  3) Collect the minimum viable evidence to speed runtime triage.

Scope / definitions
- “TP hang”: a subset of requests (or an entire pool) stops making forward progress under sustained load. Common customer-visible symptoms:
  - streaming responses stall mid-stream (client sees open connection, no new tokens)
  - requests time out at gateway / upstream (504) or runtime returns 5xx after internal timeout
  - queue depth grows while GPU utilization may look ‘normal’ or ‘stuck’
- Failure domain we care about operationally:
  - TP group (set of ranks participating in collectives)
  - Host / node (single GPU host in a dedicated pool)
  - Pool / region (Hosted large pools)

Who to page / escalation map
- Immediate responders: SRE primary + incident commander (IC) if impact is customer-visible.
- Runtime escalation:
  - Runtime Scheduling oncall (Sofia Ivanova’s rotation / scheduler)
  - Runtime Kernels/Collectives oncall (Hiro Tanaka’s rotation / kernels)
- Release coordination: Connor O’Brien (if mitigation involves config rollout or hotfix).
- Support/CS: Dev Patel / Owen Phillips (if Dedicated customer impact).

Fast classification: comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation
Use the dashboard + logs (links above). Quick heuristics:
- Likely collective/comm stall (NCCL-ish):
  - collective latency histograms show long tail or ‘flatline high’
  - per-rank progress diverges (some ranks progress, one rank stuck)
  - errors may not surface promptly; retries don’t resolve
- Likely scheduler/barrier/cancellation deadlock:
  - spikes correlate with streaming disconnects / client cancels / request timeouts
  - queue depth increases but GPUs not fully utilized
  - a specific TP group shows zero progress while host is otherwise healthy
- Likely kernel stall:
  - GPU SM utilization stuck high with no token output
  - host-level watchdog / GPU reset events (if present)
  - repeated stalls on specific model + seq-len mix

Paging thresholds (proposed defaults; tune per region after 1–2 weeks of signal)
Note: thresholds assume we page for “stuckness” (no forward progress), not just “slow”.

1) Customer impact alerts
- Hosted pools:
  - Page if 5xx rate (runtime + gateway) > 1% for 5m AND at least 30% of errors are timeout-related.
  - Page if p95 end-to-end latency > 2x baseline for 10m AND request queue depth continues rising.
- Dedicated clusters:
  - Page if any single Dedicated customer has > 2% timeouts for 5m OR > 20 concurrent streams stalled > 60s.

2) TP health alerts (preferred / earlier detection)
- Page if “TP-group watchdog triggers” > 3 triggers in 10m in a single pool OR > 1 trigger affecting > 5% of capacity.
- Page if “TP-group resets/quarantines” exceed 1% of requests in 15m (indicates widespread instability).
- Page if per-rank progress skew: any rank in a TP group shows zero progress for > 30s while peers advance for > 30s (requires instrumentation; see ‘SRE needs from Runtime’).

3) Noise suppression / lower-sev
- Ticket (not page) if watchdog triggers occur but no customer-visible error-rate increase and overall token throughput is stable.

Immediate mitigations (choose the least disruptive first)
Ordered playbook: shift traffic / shed load → quarantine/unhealthy group handling → disable risky features → node/pool restart.

A) Shed load / reduce concurrency (fastest, lowest risk)
- Reduce max concurrent streams per worker / per TP group (config push via runtime config service).
- Reduce max input tokens / max total tokens temporarily for affected pools (protects long-running streams).
- Enable stricter backpressure: reject/429 when queue depth > threshold to prevent overload collapse.

B) Traffic steering
- Hosted:
  - Shift traffic away from affected pool/region (standard traffic manager runbook).
  - If model routing allows, route to a smaller model variant or to non-TP deployment for that model temporarily.
- Dedicated:
  - If customer has multi-zone capacity: shift traffic to healthy zone/pool.

C) Quarantine / reset behavior (requires runtime support)
- If TP-group quarantine is available:
  - Ensure scheduler stops assigning new work to quarantined TP groups.
  - Trigger controlled teardown/recreate of the TP group (prefer graceful abort of in-flight requests with explicit error over silent hang).
- If quarantine is NOT available:
  - Remove unhealthy hosts from rotation (cordon) and recycle them.

D) Feature / config mitigations (use when symptoms match known signatures)
- Streaming cancellation deadlock suspected:
  - Increase server-side tolerance to client disconnects (avoid immediate barrier waits on cancel path) OR temporarily disable “eager cancel” behavior if feature-flagged.
- Collective timeout / async error propagation suspected:
  - Reduce collective timeout threshold only if it helps fail-fast (avoid too low causing false positives). Prefer enabling periodic async error checks if feature-flagged.
- As last resort:
  - Temporarily disable TP for the affected model in that pool (falls back to single-GPU or smaller model). Communicate performance impact.

E) Restart / recycle
- Host-level restart (Dedicated): recycle the specific node(s) showing stuck groups; preserve evidence first (see “Evidence to collect”).
- Pool-level recycle (Hosted): coordinate with Runtime + Releases; do not mass-restart without guardrails (risk of thundering herd + capacity loss).

Incident Commander guidance (checklist)
1) Declare severity
- SEV1: widespread Hosted impact (multi-tenant, elevated 5xx/timeouts across pools) OR Dedicated enterprise outage (>50% request failure, production down).
- SEV2: single pool degradation with partial mitigation available; limited Dedicated impact with workaround.
- SEV3: intermittent watchdog triggers with minimal customer impact.

2) Stabilize first
- Prefer traffic shifting + load shedding over experimental config changes.
- Pick ONE mitigation lever at a time; note timestamp and expected outcome window (5–10m).

3) Communications
- Start internal incident channel with:
  - affected pools/regions, model(s), start time, current error rate, mitigation in progress
  - link to dashboard panels (collectives latency, watchdog triggers, resets, 5xx)
- If Dedicated customer affected:
  - notify Support/CS with a clear summary and ETA for next update (15–30m cadence during SEV1/SEV2).

4) Escalate with crisp ask
- To Runtime Scheduling:
  - “We suspect scheduler/barrier/cancel deadlock. Need guidance on safe flags + whether to enable quarantine/reset in pool X.”
- To Kernels/Collectives:
  - “Collective latency flatlining + per-rank skew suggests comm stall. Need confirmation of async error checks + recommended timeout values.”

5) Exit criteria
- We can downgrade/resolve when:
  - error rates return to baseline for 30m
  - watchdog triggers stop (or remain below noise threshold)
  - queue depth normalizes and token throughput stable

Evidence to collect (minimum viable; don’t block mitigation)
Collect within first 10–15 minutes if possible:
- Pool/cluster identifiers: region, pool name, runtime version, model version, GPU type/driver.
- Dashboard snapshots (timestamps):
  - collective latency histogram panel
  - per-rank progress panel (if available)
  - watchdog triggers + resets
  - request queue depth + p95 latency + 5xx/timeouts
- Representative request IDs: 5–10 stalled streams + 5–10 timeouts.
- Logs:
  - structured “collective stall” logs (rank id, op, duration, tp_group_id)
  - scheduler starvation / barrier wait logs
- If Dedicated: customer-provided timestamps + any client-side timeout values.

What SRE needs from Runtime (requirements / gaps)
This section is the contract we need to operate this safely.

1) Signals / metrics (pool + tp_group granularity)
- tp_group_forward_progress_seconds (gauge): seconds since last completed forward step per tp_group.
- tp_group_watchdog_trigger_total (counter) with labels: model, pool, tp_group_id, reason (no_progress, collective_timeout, async_error_detected).
- collective_latency_ms (histogram) with labels: op (allreduce/allgather/reducescatter), tp_size, model.
- per_rank_progress_tokens_total (counter) or equivalent “step id” marker per rank.
- tp_group_quarantined (gauge) + tp_group_reset_total (counter).
- request_cancellation_total with labels: client_disconnect, server_timeout, upstream_cancel.

2) Control knobs (feature flags with safe defaults)
- Enable/disable:
  - tp_group_quarantine
  - periodic async error checks for collectives
  - watchdog sensitivity (threshold seconds, number of consecutive violations)
- Load knobs:
  - max concurrent streams per worker
  - max total tokens / max input tokens overrides per pool
- Routing knobs:
  - per-model “disable TP” emergency switch (time-bounded)

3) Safe failure semantics
- When watchdog triggers: fail fast + explicit error code to upstream (avoid silent hang).
- Ensure scheduler will not schedule new work onto quarantined tp groups.
- Ensure reset does not wedge the entire host process (define blast radius).

4) Runbook links embedded in alerts
- Every TP health alert should link to:
  - the TP health dashboard
  - the debugging playbook
  - the recommended mitigations list (this doc)

Known risky scenarios (as of Feb/Mar 2025)
- High concurrency + long-running streaming + mixed sequence lengths (very long + very short) appears to increase likelihood of TP group skew.
- Elevated client disconnects (mobile networks / aggressive client timeouts) can amplify cancel-path stress.
- “Overload collapse”: once a few tp groups are stuck, scheduler continues assigning work → queue growth → more timeouts → more cancels → feedback loop.

Post-incident follow-ups (SRE-owned checklist)
- Create incident ticket with:
  - timeline, mitigation actions + timestamps, capacity impact
  - which signals were missing / unclear
  - estimate of affected requests (timeouts + hung streams)
- File/attach evidence to Runtime umbrella issue (ENG-2401) and link the incident channel.
- If Dedicated customer impacted:
  - ensure Support has a customer-ready summary of mitigations applied and what will change in the next runtime release.

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm final paging thresholds once tp_group watchdog metrics are rolled out broadly (need baseline false positive rate).
- Decide standard customer-facing error mapping for “tp_group quarantined / reset in progress” (avoid confusing generic 5xx).
- Clarify ownership for pool-wide “disable TP” toggle approvals during SEV1 (SRE vs Runtime vs Release manager).
